caption:
is hypochlorous acid spray good for your skin?

Hypochlorous acid (HOCl) is the face mist all over TikTok. It is also a molecule your own immune cells make - neutrophils and macrophages produce it to kill microbes. In wound care it is valued for being antimicrobial while generally well tolerated.

Where the evidence is strongest: wounds. A 2026 review of one pure HOCl wound cleanser pulled together 56 publications and 2,682 patients, including newborns, with no product-related complications reported. Two of its authors work for the manufacturer.

Where it is thinner: everyday face use for acne, redness or "calming". A 2025 review across specialties found it useful in most studies, but noted the results are not entirely consistent and the right dosing is not settled.

One practical point: these products are not all the same. How much of a bottle is true hypochlorous acid, and how much is hypochlorite, depends on pH and how it was made - and it can drift over time. Storage matters.

What this does not mean: a mist is not a replacement for acne treatment. If you like how one feels, fine. Just don't expect it to do the job of one.
